description: Stereo delay in four HP with a separate time for each side, and a chaotic signal generated inside it that can drift both times and the feedback

params.text: Sets the delay on the left side, 1ms to 2 seconds
Sets the delay on the right side, 1ms to 2 seconds
Sets how much of the delayed signal is written back into the line, 0% to 95%
Crossfades between the signal coming in and the delayed signal, 0% for the dry signal alone and 100% for the delay alone
Sets how deeply the chaotic signal drifts the two delay times and the feedback, 0% to 100%; at zero all three hold where the knobs put them
Sets how fast the chaotic signal moves, a hundredth of its base speed to twice it

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to be delayed; with nothing patched to the right jack this one feeds both sides
The right side of the signal to be delayed
Added to the TIME L knob, a fifth of a second per volt; the total is held between 1ms and 2 seconds
Added to the TIME R knob, a fifth of a second per volt; the total is held between 1ms and 2 seconds
Added to the FEEDBACK knob, ten points of feedback per volt; the total is held between 0% and 95%
Added to the MIX knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the CHAOS knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the RATE knob, a fifth of the base speed per volt; the total is held between a hundredth of it and twice it

outputs.text: The left side of the delay, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The right side of the delay, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The chaotic signal itself, ±5V, at the speed set by RATE; the CHAOS knob does not dim it
The chaotic signal sampled and held ten times per unit of the RATE setting, ±5V; the CHAOS knob does not dim it

notes: place this immediately to the right of a YAMANOTE and cables appear on their own: YAMANOTE's send A into the two input jacks, and the two output jacks into its return A.
placing it to the right of another Runner, Facehugger or Ovomorph that is itself beside a YAMANOTE cables it to that YAMANOTE's send and return B instead.
the chaotic signal is a three-variable system that runs whether or not the CHAOS knob is up, so the two CV outputs carry a signal even at a CHAOS setting of zero.
